newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Bamerindus denies change in ownership.
newsitem.headline: Bamerindus denies change in ownership.

text.p: Brazilian private bank Bamerindus denied Monday a news report saying control of the bank would be transferred to a group of executives, according to a statement sent to the Sao Paulo Stock Exchange (Bovespa).

The statement followed a request by the bourse asking for clarification on a Folha de Sao Paulo report Saturday that the government would finance a group of executives who would take over the troubled bank for a certain period of time.
According to Folha, this group would hire a private bank to help clean up Bamerindus' balance sheets and find buyers for the bank within two years.
"We do not confirm the report published in the Folha de Sao Paulo daily's edition of November 30," the bank said in the statement.
Bamerindus' denial led the bourse to resume trade in the bank's shares as of 1600 local time/1800 GMT. Trade in the shares had been suspended earlier today, a bourse spokesman said.
For months Bamerindus, Brazil's fourth largest private bank, has been subject of speculation that the bank would be sold due to its widely-known liquidity troubles.
